The new w4a16_kernels.py defined a Triton kernel with one program per output-column tile. # Unpack: low nibble -> k=0,2,4..; high nibble -> k=1,3,...
w_lo = (wq & 0xF).to(tl.int32)
w_hi = ((wq >> 4) & 0xF).to(tl.int32)

# Interleave to [BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N]
w = tl.join(w_lo, w_hi)  # [BLOCK_K/2, 2, BLOCK_N]
w = tl.reshape(w, (BLOCK_K, BLOCK_N))

The official H100 result is timeout, correct=false, with no score; the audit records a failed output cosine of 0.2377 against the required 0.98.

Relevant prior context

The run first found that the default Python environment lacked PyTorch, then set up the project environment. The available device was an H100 PCIe, while the brief described an RTX PRO 6000 target. A basic step smoke check passed. The baseline measured 12.232 ms/tok at context 2048.

The standalone GEMV work made progress: an initial nibble unpacking error gave cosine 0.0364; after correcting the Triton join layout, GEMV cosine reached about 0.995. A tuning sweep reported block_n=32, num_warps=2 at 32.3 us, and later a best shown configuration of bn=16 nw=1 ns=3: 26.4 us. These are component measurements, not end-to-end solution performance.

KDA was isolated and matched the reference (KDA only output and state cosine 1.0000). The MLA cache update also matched (c_kv cos: 1.0000), but MLA output and MoE output did not. The MoE gate and up projections matched in focused checks; the down projection output was much smaller than reference.

Important non-obvious context

The task required exactly one custom GPU kernel launch for a timed step. The submitted Model.step instead loops over four blocks and invokes separate Triton GEMVs and PyTorch operations for projections, routing, softmax, attention, state updates, and MoE. It therefore does not implement the required one-launch megakernel, independent of its correctness failure.

The grouped GEMV kernel loads its input as a single shared vector, using x_ptr + k_offs * stride_x. That is suitable for gate/up projections, which share the hidden vector across selected experts. The MoE down path passes hh with shape [n_active, moe_inter], where every expert has its own input row. The kernel does not index that input by expert, and its stride_x is set from x.stride(0). This is incompatible with the per-expert layout and explains why the down projection failed. The same grouped helper is also used for shared-expert down projection with a two-dimensional input.

The brief defines speedup as baseline latency divided by solution latency and reports the geomean in peak_fraction; correctness is required before a valid speedup is available. This run has no valid speedup.

Recording summary

The submitted code defines custom W4A16 GEMV and grouped GEMV kernels. The core grouped kernel uses an input load that assumes one shared vector for all expert programs:

x_even = tl.load(x_ptr + k_offs_even * stride_x, mask=k_mask_even, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
x_odd = tl.load(x_ptr + k_offs_odd * stride_x, mask=k_mask_odd, other=0.0).to(tl.float32)
